why.evolution and setup: Every attacker is a Stage 1 (Mega Sharpedo ex from Carvanha, Wailord from Wailmer, Claydol from Baltoy); Wallace evolves a 50-HP Water Basic straight from the deck and Elegant Cape gives +30 HP only to Stage 1s.
why.Bench preparation: Turbo Shark puts zone Water on a Benched Water Pokémon and Whale Pump gets +10 per Water, so Wailord is charged on the Bench; Capes and Heavy Helmet go on benched Basics before they evolve.
why.sacrifice and recovery: Mega Sharpedo ex is a 3-point Mega with retreat 0, so it is pulled back when damaged, and walls (Wailmer/Wailord, retreat 3-4, with Heavy Helmet's -20) or Carvanha/Baltoy take 1-point knockouts in front.
why.fast pressure: Wallace can make Mega Sharpedo ex on turn 1-2, and Turbo Shark does 70 for a single Water, so it hits from the first turn it has Energy.

why.control and combinations: Damage and denial come from combos: Deceptive Needle's end-of-turn 10, Poison Barb, Weezing ex's Boiler Smog (Poison+Burn), Goo-zooka's retreat tax, Alolan Muk's Basic-Ability lock, Claydol's Heal Block, Cursed Jewel's retaliation, Cyrus and Field Blower.
why.evolution and setup: Alolan Muk, Team Rocket's Weezing ex (ability only when evolving) and Claydol are Stage 1s that must be benched and evolved, while Mega Sableye ex and Hoopa ex need two or three Darkness built up.
